title: Red Flags for Phone Call Scams
summary: Red Flags for Phone Call Scams
body_markdown:

October 16, 2026


## Red Flags for Phone Call Scams


**Has someone claiming to be from the bank told you there is fraud on your account, or that a Bank Employee is stealing your money?**


They may ask you to move your money to a "safe account" or send cash or wires.


**Has someone claiming to be from the bank asked you to share a one-time passcode sent to your device or a code from your security token?**


This is a common tactic used by scammers to gain access to your accounts.


**Has someone contacted you claiming you owe money to the government, or that you will be arrested or in legal trouble if you don't pay?**


Scammers pretend to be from the IRS, Social Security, law enforcement, or other agencies.


**Has someone claiming to be tech support or a customer service representative remotely accessed your computer or device so they could “assist” you?**


Legitimate companies do not need to connect to your computer or device.


**Has someone contacted you claiming a family member is in danger or in jail and asked you to send money to help them?**


Scammers use fear to get you to act without thinking.


**Has someone you have never met claimed to be romantically interested in you and asked you to send money or help them financially?**


Romance scams are very common and can happen to anyone.


**Has someone told you to keep this a secret or not to tell anyone about this transaction?**


Scammers don't want you to talk to family, friends, or your bank.


**Has someone pressured you to act quickly or said you must do this right now to avoid problems?**


They create urgency so you won't have time to think.


**Has someone you don't know sent someone to your home or asked you to meet somewhere to give them money or pick up money or other items?**


This includes meeting in a parking lot or other public place.


**Have you been asked to invest in cryptocurrency, gold futures, or other investments that you don't fully understand?**


Scammers promise high returns but steal your money.


**Has someone asked you to wire money to a person or company you have never met or to lie about the purpose of the wire (for example, say it's for "house renovations")?**


Never send money or wire funds to someone you don't know and trust, Legitimate transactions should never require to misrepresent the purpose of the transaction.


**Has someone contacted you claiming you won a prize or lottery and asked you to pay fees or taxes to claim it?**


You can't win a prize for a contest you didn't enter.


**Are you being asked to liquidate your accounts, send cash, or wire money to secure your accounts or clear you of a crime?**


This is a scam. The bank or government will never ask you to do this.


### MAKE SURE IT'S REALLY US


Fraudsters may pose as representatives of Virginia National Bank.


Virginia National Bank will NEVER ask our clients to provide your:


- Personal Identification Number (PIN) or security codes
- Bank account information
- Personal information once your account is opened


**We will NEVER ask you to send payments anywhere.**
